why: This catalog mirrors metadata for Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs hosted by the Microsoft Planetary Computer. It does not host the scene bytes or the referenced thumbnail bytes, so it cannot publish a file:checksum for either. Since spec PR #116 that is conformant rather than a gap. PORTO-CORE-028 makes both file fields SHOULD, and PORTO-CORE-030 asks only that a value an asset does carry match the bytes its href resolves to, which a fabricated digest would violate. rashid reports the absence at warning severity. This file records the one warning that is expected, so a new one still fails the gate.
data_scope_why: rashid's default data pass streams every asset in full, which here is 1.86 TB of COGs hosted by the Microsoft Planetary Computer. --data-scope local, added by portolan-sdi/rashid#87 answering the rashid#86 filed from this work, runs every data rule but treats a remote href as unfetchable. So this is not a skipped pass. The Collection's own local assets, items.parquet above all, are fully checked for checksum, size, format, spatial ordering, per-row-group statistics and row-per-item parity. What stays unchecked is the bytes of the 1848 remote assets, which no gate here has ever read and which PTL-AST-003 below already records as unverified.
matching_why: Each entry pins an exact count, a severity, a path glob and a message glob, and all of them have to match before a finding counts as known. An exact count fails in both directions, which is the point. Downward it catches an upstream search returning fewer scenes than it should, and a gutted catalog being published over the good one by s5cmd sync --delete. Upward it catches a second asset losing its checksum. The severity has to match too, so PTL-AST-003 returning to error, which is what a spec change back to MUST would do, reads as a regression rather than a match. The path glob keeps a rule accepted for remote assets from also excusing itself on items.parquet, a file this project does host and must checksum. The message glob keeps the same rule failing for a new reason, a bad file:size rather than an absent checksum, from passing as known.
recount_how: The count follows from the scene count, so it moves whenever upstream adds or drops a scene. That is a deliberate review point rather than a nuisance. PTL-AST-003 is 2 per Item, one for the scene COG and one for the referenced upstream thumbnail, so the number is twice the scene count. Note where the new number appears. build.py validates each catalog as it finishes, through validate.py, using this same matcher, so a changed scene count fails the build step and check_catalogs.py never runs. Read the observed total off the UNEXPECTED lines there, each of which names what a rule occurred and what the baseline expected, rather than waiting for the 'baseline accepts' summary that only a completed gate run prints. Then update the count in the same commit that explains why the scene count changed.

accepted.why: file:checksum is omitted on the scene COG asset and on the referenced upstream thumbnail asset, because this catalog does not host either. Computing one means reading 1.86 TB, summed from the file:size of every built item, and inventing one would assert something about bytes never read, which PORTO-CORE-030 forbids. PORTO-CORE-028 makes the field a SHOULD, so the omission conforms and rashid scores it a warning. Reported per asset, so 2 per Item across 924 Items.
